full_judgment: 9. The undisputed position is that land measuring 45 decimals described in the 'ka' schedule belonged to Yakub Ali. He sold the same in March 12, 1977 to his son Ishaque who sold said 45 decimals of land to the plaintiff-appellant on December 1, 1977. Since defendant was in occupation of 4½ decimals of land, shown in the sketch map attached to the plaint, part of 22 decimals of land of plot No. 1063 (new), 1330 (old), fully described in 'Kha' schedule and the defendant having not surrendered possession in favour of the plaintiff in fulfilment of his earlier commitment, as asserted by the plaintiff, he filed the suit for recovery of possession of 4½ decimals of land. The case of the defendant was that his father allowed him to stay in the land in respect whereof the decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession has been prayed by the plaintiff and he is possessing the land by erecting a hut. It was also his case that the kabala executed and registered by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon. It may be mentioned while plaintiff filed the suit seeking declaration of title and recovery of khas possession Yakub Ali had died. The suit initially was dismissed by the trial Court as stated herein before and on appeal the Court upon allowing the appeal remanded the suit back to the trial Court with the direction to the plaintiff to amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition.
